references.text: Washing of clothes as part of the cleansing process for leprosy is also mentioned here.
The continuation of the cleansing ritual on the seventh day, with repeated shaving, washing of clothes, and bathing.
The Levites' cleansing also included shaving the entire body and washing their clothes.
Miriam was shut out of the camp for seven days because of leprosy, similar to the seven-day isolation mentioned here.
The leper had to live outside the camp, and this verse describes reentry after cleansing.
A similar cleansing ritual involving washing of clothes and bathing in water to become clean.
Reference to following the priests' instructions regarding leprosy.
Naaman was told to wash seven times to be cleansed from his leprosy.
Jesus sent the healed leper to the priest to carry out what Moses had commanded, which includes the ritual in Leviticus 14.
Jesus sent the ten lepers to the priests for cleansing according to the Law of Moses.
